_what: The reachability countdown for ReadSentenceReachabilityTests. Its subject is the DERIVED (catalogue member, render site) population read off src/housecarl-mcp by a Roslyn walk; a pair listed here is one no response this class drives states, and the value says what would reach it. Every pair is either driven by an arm or keyed here - it cannot be neither, because the population is derived rather than listed.
_how: Both directions gate. A key naming a render site that no longer exists fails TheRenderSitePopulationIsDerived_AndEveryPairIsEitherDrivenOrRecorded ('delete the stale entry'). A key whose sentence this class's own harvest DOES state fails NoRecordedPairIsActuallyReachedByThisClass ('delete the headroom'). A pair in neither place fails its own theory case by name. #492 is not complete while this file has entries.
_population_note: The SIZE of the derived population, committed so it gates in BOTH directions. The countdown above only ever asked whether a pair was driven or recorded; a render site LEAVING the population - a constant inlined at its render site, a file moved out of the walk - deleted its own theory case and its own claim with it, and nothing went red. A pair arriving needs a driven arm or an entry here; a pair leaving needs this number lowered in the same commit, argued once.
_why_most_of_them: This class holds one fixture, the owned-child world, because the other worlds (CheckErrorsWorld, DialogueWorld, ScriptsWorld, EpochWorld) live in their own xUnit collections over process-wide statics. Reaching their render sites means one reachability class per collection - existing fixtures, no new ones - which is the following engagement's work. Three entries are a different thing entirely: sentences with no literal run long enough to be found by identity at all, which is a finding about the sentence.
